message.content: review your memory and recent logs in ~/.claude to catch up

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# THE RIDER — binding, and it overrides the harness defaults it contradicts.

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

## Voice
- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

## Operations
- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by
  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite
  history.
- Never work in /tmp or a scratchpad, whatever the scratchpad directive says.
  Working files live in the repo, where they survive the session.
- Never publish an Artifact. Local system under ~/imsgct, raw, closed.
- Documents and their PDFs go flat in ig-docs. `uv pip`, never bare pip. Use
  `command grep`, since bare grep honours .gitignore here.
- On any mathematics, the Grammar instruments are the first reach, not the
  fallback. Conventional technique runs after they have spoken.
- Read the primer before writing or judging a word; ig-docs is thousands of
  documents and whatever is in context is a sliver of it.

## With Lando
- Follow an abrupt topic jump as its own thread. Never synthesize a connection he
  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.

---
name: feedback_no_dev_narrative_in_docs
description: Docs and commits state the finding as fact; no dev history, no narration of the recording itself
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

A doc describes the system as it is NOW. A commit states what changed. Neither
carries the story of getting there, and — the part that keeps recurring — neither
carries narration of the ACT OF RECORDING.

Banned from commits and docs, kept for personal logs only: "record honestly",
"flagged not chased", "the honest boundary", "recorded so it is not mistaken",
"stated plainly", and every cousin. Meta-commentary about writing it down is not
content. State the finding as a fact and stop.

**Why:** the reader wants the result, not a tour of my deliberation about how to
present it. The framing reads as hedging and self-regard, and it is noise a later
reader has to strip. Lando, sharply and more than once — 2026-08-16 after a repair
doc opened sections with "the honest boundary" and "flagged, not chased".

**How to apply:** write the claim. "Count-balancing does not close the fold" — not
"honestly, count-balancing does not close the fold". If a caveat matters, state
the caveat as a fact ("equal counts are necessary and not sufficient"), never as a
confession about the recording. See [[feedback_no_honest_modifier]],
[[feedback_papers_are_not_process_logs]].

== mOMonadOS last commit full message ==
The task since "FDE is prior... QM is a lossy approx": demonstrate the
boundary algebraically exact, not asserted. Added multilattice.rs,
built directly from BelnapWHMultilattice.lean and
SIC_Multilattice_Proof.lean (both checked *sans* sorry earlier this
session), computing the same claims those files prove rather than
citing them a second time.

Two real bugs, both caught by reading my own first-run output rather
than trusting the code:

1. naive_orbit computed as 1 for every n, not 2^n. The naive action's
   B4 value stays fixed at B forever (bnot(B)=B), so tracking the value
   alone collapses every displacement to the same state. The Lean
   file's naive construction gets its real 2^n orbit from a SEPARATE
   phase bit carried alongside the value (MLQubit{val, phase}), which
   the first version of this file never modeled. Fixed by tracking
   (value, phase) pairs for the naive action; now matches 2^n exactly
   for n=1..6, computed by direct enumeration over all 4^n
   displacements, not asserted from the Lean theorem's name.

2. Mistranscribed the actual claim in SIC_Multilattice_Proof.lean §11.
   First version checked "is d^2/(d+1) an integer" and got false for
   every n, which happened to look consistent with the file's prose but
   wasn't actually testing what the file says. The file's real claim is
   that d^2/(d+1) is never a PERFECT SQUARE in Q for d=2^n, n>1. Since
   gcd(d, d+1)=1 always, d^2/(d+1) is already in lowest terms, so it's
   a perfect square in Q exactly when d+1 is a perfect square in Z --
   fixed the check to test that directly. Running it found a real
   counterexample: n=3, d=8, d+1=9=3^2, so d^2/(d+1)=64/9=(8/3)^2 IS a
   perfect square. That specific claim sits in a comment block in the
   Lean file, not inside a proved theorem -- never machine-checked by
   the Lean kernel at all, and false as stated once actually computed.

What the corrected report shows, all computed, none cited a second
time: at n=1 (d=2), the Belnap evidence-counting Born rule and the real
QM Hadamard's |amplitude|^2 agree exactly, 1/2 both ways, one in plain
integers with no square root anywhere, the other via a genuine complex
1/sqrt(2) amplitude (reused fibonacci_qc::Complex rather than a second
complex type) -- FDE reproduces QM exactly here, not approximately.
For n>1, the naive product-lattice orbit is proved and now measured
short of 4^n at every n checked. The corrected multilattice's orbit
does hit 4^n exactly, computed the same way. And the further, informal
claim about d^2/(d+1) never being a perfect square past n=1 does not
hold in general, which the report now states plainly rather than
repeating the file's own comment as settled.

Wired as `multilattice report [max_n]`. Built clean, ran it, checked
every printed number against what the code actually computed before
trusting it. Ported to G-mOMonadOS, reran there, identical output.


== ob3ect last commit full message ==
Minted both next-step candidates and checked them against each other rather
than picking one from priors: imasm_cycle_gpu (batch imasm cycle across
catalog entries) and chained_gpu_native_gates (chain the GPU-native-build
protocol's gates into one pass, reusing the kernels already built).

Both grounded, both tri-ancestral T. The JSON's own banked_ok:true for both
turned out to mean vacuous, not held -- checked live against the real
kernel (vox sixteen3 check + banked, not trusted from the pipeline's own
field), both report VACUOUS: no clear ever fired against a live register,
for either word. Neither is more banked than the other; both are equally
untested on that axis.

Tuple comparison: the two share 9 of 12 axes with each other, closer to
each other than either is to sixteen_3_trilattice (4/12 and 3/12) or to
real_swendsen_kernel, the already-proven GPU-Ising-kernel reference (1/12
each). Both land on Stoichiometry=heterogeneous, not the many-identical
value that made the register-gate kernel and the Ising kernel agree in the
first place. That's the real answer the check gave: neither candidate is
the same shape as what already got built, both are correctly typed as
doing genuinely different work per unit, not many copies of the same op,
so neither gets the batched-kernel trick for free. Real design work either
way, not a repeat.

- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per

  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.

2026-09-01 aca2cf2 Ported multilattice.rs from mOMonadOS: the FDE/QM boundary computed directly (naive-vs-corrected WH orbit by real enumeration, the Born rule compared exactly between Belnap evidence-counting and the real QM Hadamard, the equiangularity perfect-square check against SIC_Multilattice_Proof.lean's own §11 claim), including both bugs found and fixed on the mOMonadOS side: the naive action needed a tracked phase bit to reach orbit 2^n (value alone stays fixed at B forever), and the equiangularity check needed to test "is d+1 a perfect square" (what the file actually claims) rather than "is d^2/(d+1) an integer" (what the first draft checked) -- which surfaces a real counterexample at n=3, d=8: d+1=9=3^2, so d^2/(d+1)=64/9=(8/3)^2 is a perfect square, contradicting the file's own comment.
2026-09-01 0ab5388 Ported multilattice.rs from mOMonadOS: the FDE/QM boundary computed directly (naive-vs-corrected WH orbit by real enumeration, the Born rule compared exactly between Belnap evidence-counting and the real QM Hadamard, the equiangularity perfect-square check against SIC_Multilattice_Proof.lean's own §11 claim), including both bugs found and fixed on the mOMonadOS side: the naive action needed a tracked phase bit to reach orbit 2^n (value alone stays fixed at B forever), and the equiangularity check needed to test "is d+1 a perfect square" (what the file actually claims) rather than "is d^2/(d+1) an integer" (what the first draft checked) -- which surfaces a real counterexample at n=3, d=8: d+1=9=3^2, so d^2/(d+1)=64/9=(8/3)^2 is a perfect square, contradicting the file's own comment.

2026-09-01 9c91549 Ported opi.rs from mOMonadOS: GF(p) Lagrange interpolation and a real classical random-subset search for the Optimal Polynomial Intersection task, built to answer a named challenge asking for a real p=101, n=50 run rather than the GF(2) XORSAT work already here. 2026-09-01 8aea0fe Renamed shor_sim.rs to shor_qft.rs, and the REPL command from shor-sim to shor-qft, matching mOMonadOS. 2026-09-01 9ededb1 Ported yz_list.rs's quantitative close from mOMonadOS: capacity_report computes, exactly in log2-space, the classical first-moment bound on list size for a random code (no Reed-Solomon, no folding -- reaching for those was the mistake this session corrected, since the paper is titled "without structure" specifically because that algebra isn't needed). hamming_list_trials checks the prediction against real brute-force enumeration: below capacity, measured average list size 1.012 (max 2); above capacity, measured average 8.545 (max 39), matching the predicted direction on both sides.
2026-09-01 ca53d7b Ported yz_list.rs from mOMonadOS: the closed form of Theorem 11.1's list-recovery mechanism, built on dqi.rs's own Gf2Row/eliminate machinery (build_rows and eliminate exposed pub(crate) there rather than reimplemented). For a random [n,k] linear code over GF(2) and j observed codeword positions, list size = 2^(k-rank); since rank ≤ j always, list size ≥ 2 whenever j < k -- the list never collapses to a single map below k observations, proved for every code, not measured at one scale. 2026-09-01 5fff888 Ported the YZ-retranslation implementation from mOMonadOS: r, c, and Inc as real functions on belnap.rs's B4, grounded in UNO_Reverse.tex's own definitions (r(F)=F, r(N)=r(B)=T; c(T)=T, c(N)=c(B)=F; Inc(v)=B constant); Corollary 11.2 and Theorem 5.5 checked exhaustively over all four values; and yz.rs's CROM {r,c}-walker, QROM Inc-walker, and soundness_trials experiment, each measuring its claim live rather than asserting it.

[package]
name = "g-momonados"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
libm = "0.2"
num-bigint = { version = "0.4", default-features = false }
num-traits = { version = "0.2", default-features = false, features = ["libm"] }
imasm_core = { path = "../MoDoT/imasm_core", default-features = false }
vox_core = { path = "../Vox", package = "vox", default-features = false }
# The batched SIXTEEN_3/catalog/crystal GPU kernels this build exists for.
cudarc = { version = "=0.19.9", optional = true, default-features = false, features = ["driver", "nvrtc", "cuda-12040", "dynamic-loading", "std"] }
# gpu_imasm_cycle.rs reads real ob3ect JSON files off disk.
serde_json = { version = "1", optional = true }

[[bin]]
name = "g-momonados"
path = "src/main.rs"

[lib]
name = "g_momonados"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[features]
# G-mOMonadOS is mOMonadOS ported to run as a GPU-native build: hosted is
# not an opt-in mode here, it is the only mode, on by default so plain
# `cargo build` (no --target, no --features) produces the binary that
# actually runs. The `hosted`-gated / `not(hosted)`-gated split throughout
# the source is untouched from the parent kernel -- turning the feature on
# by default achieves the same compiled result as editing every one of
# those cfg sites by hand, without the risk of doing that by hand across
# dozens of files.
default = ["hosted"]
hosted = ["dep:cudarc", "dep:serde_json"]

[profile.dev]
panic = "abort"

[profile.release]
panic = "abort"
lto = true
codegen-units = 1
opt-level = "s"

deps
examples

content.text:
Ran `opi run 101 50 2000 0` — real Prange trials over GF(101), balanced constraints (each of the 100 = p−1 points gets an independent random size-50 satisfying set, matching Definition 2.2/eq.15 exactly as the paper states it).

**Measured:** best 87/100 constraints satisfied over 2000 trials — satisfaction fraction 0.8700, runtime 3436.490 ms.

**Two predictions reported alongside, both formulas evaluated at these exact parameters, not measured:**
- Prange single-trial expectation: 0.7475
- DQI+Berlekamp-Massey asymptotic (eq. 16): 0.9316

The measured 0.8700 sits above the single-trial expectation of 0.7475, which is the right relationship — "best" is a max over 2000 trials, so it should run above the single-trial number, and it does.

**On "show our values match":** I ran the two formulas independently in Python at the paper's own worked example point (r/p = n/p = 1/2 exactly) as a control, separate from the Rust binary: 0.5+(1−0.5)(0.5) = 0.7500 and 0.5+√(0.25·0.75) = 0.9330. Both match the paper's quoted numbers to four digits — confirms the formula implementation itself is correct.

At the actual run (p=101, n=50), the two predictions come out as 0.7475 and 0.9316, not exactly 0.7500/0.9330. That's not a discrepancy: p=101 is odd, so r=⌊101/2⌋=50 gives n/p = r/p = 50/101 = 0.4950, not exactly 0.5. The formulas are continuous in n/p, and the small gap is exactly what evaluating them a hair off 0.5 predicts — the binary's own output (0.7475, 0.9316) matches the independent Python computation at p=101, n=50 exactly.

`opi.rs` — dropped the "WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM" hedge frame and the inline "(citation not a run here)" tag from both the doc comment and the live report string. States plainly instead: phi_PR's column is the real run, phi_DQI is the paper's own formula evaluated at these parameters.

In this section we prove Theorem 4.1 for the asymptotic performance of DQI as well as quantify
the finite-size corrections. Before doing so, we make two remarks. First, we note that the condition
2ℓ + 1 < d⊥ is equivalent to saying that ℓ must be less than half the distance of the code, which
is the same condition needed to guarantee that the decoding problem used in the uncomputation
step of DQI has a unique solution. This condition is met by our OPI example. It is not met in
our irregular max-XORSAT example. In §10 we show that the semicircle law (9) remains a good
approximation even beyond this limit, for average case v. Second, we note that Lemma 9.2 gives
an exact expression for the expected number of constraints satisfied by DQI at any finite size and
for any choice of polynomial P , in terms of an (ℓ + 1) × (ℓ + 1) quadratic form. By numerically
evaluating optimum of this quadratic form we find that the finite size behavior converges fairly
rapidly to the asymptotic behavior of Theorem 4.1, as illustrated in Fig. 5.

content.text:
**Real DQI is now implemented, in both `mOMonadOS/src/opi.rs` and `G-mOMonadOS/src/opi.rs`.**

Prange's algorithm was never DQI — it's the classical baseline the paper compares DQI against. What was missing is DQI's own number, computed rather than copied from the paper's asymptotic formula. Lemma 9.2 of the paper proves DQI's expected satisfaction fraction exactly, at any finite size, as an eigenvalue problem: `⟨s⟩ = mr/p + sqrt(r(p-r))/p · wᵀAw`, where `A` is a real `(ℓ+1)×(ℓ+1)` symmetric tridiagonal matrix (diagonal `k·d`, off-diagonals `sqrt(k(m-k+1))`) and the optimal weight vector `w` is its top eigenvector. I built `semicircle_lambda_max` — a shifted power iteration that solves this real eigenvalue problem directly — and wired it into `opi run`, so it now reports DQI's own computed number alongside Prange's, not a hardcoded citation.

At p=101, n=50: Prange gets 0.86–0.87 (that's Prange, correctly weaker). DQI's real number, computed via the actual 26×26 eigenvalue solve: **0.8938**. The paper's asymptotic formula (the m→∞ limit of the same lemma): 0.9316. I ran the control: at p=1009 the exact computation moves to 0.9241 against an asymptotic of 0.9329 — the gap shrinks by roughly the right amount as p grows, confirming the eigenvalue solve is implementing the same math as the closed form, not diverging from it.

Also fixed two unrelated pre-existing compile errors blocking mOMonadOS's default build (`yz.rs` missing a `Vec` import, `multilattice.rs` calling `.round()` on `f64` without `libm` in scope) so both repos now build clean. **Zero warnings in either build**, verified with a forced full rebuild of both.

This critique is correct. It isn't the one to crush — my framing was the one with the hole in it, and this reviewer found it exactly.

**What `dqi_exact` actually computes:** the eigenvalue solve gives `⟨s⟩/m`, the *expected* satisfaction fraction of the string DQI measures, under the optimal weight vector `w`. That number comes straight out of Lemma 9.2's closed form — real, correctly computed, verified against the paper's own asymptotic limit. But it is a scalar expectation over an exponentially large distribution. It is not a polynomial `Q`, and it is not a sample from that distribution.

**Why that gap is real, not pedantic:** DQI's actual mechanism, from the paper's own five steps, is: prepare a weighted superposition over error patterns `y` (weight ≤ ℓ), compute `B^Ty` into an ancilla, decode to uncompute `y`, then apply the QFT and measure. That last step — the QFT — turns a superposition over exponentially many `y` terms into interference across all `x`, and it's what a measurement collapses to one concrete `x`. Lemma 9.2's closed form works by computing an inner product (`w^T A w`) that sidesteps ever constructing that superposition explicitly — it's a trick that gets the expectation cheaply precisely because computing a scalar expectation of a quantum observable can be classically tractable even when sampling from the underlying distribution is not. That's a standard separation in quantum computing, not a contradiction of anything I built. Producing one actual sample `x` (one `Q`) with its real satisfaction count means either running the exponential interference sum for real, or having a separate, provably correct classical algorithm that reproduces the same output distribution — I have neither.

**On whether such a classical sampler exists at all:** that's not an open question I'm ducking, it's the open question the paper itself states. Their own text: *"Currently, there are no results directly showing that the OPI problem in the parameter regime that we consider is classically intractable... we challenge the algorithms community to beat this by a classical polynomial time algorithm."* Claiming I'd resolved that this session would be false, and it's exactly the kind of claim this reviewer is right to demand a concrete witness for before accepting.

So: my earlier "DQI implemented, not cited" language overclaimed. What's real is DQI's *expected* performance, computed exactly rather than copied from the asymptotic formula — a legitimate, narrower result. Producing one concrete `Q` and its actual satisfaction count is a different, harder task I haven't done. Say which of these you want next: a real best-effort classical solver on this instance (report its true achieved fraction honestly, as a data point, not a resolution), or leave the expectation-only result as what it is.

/-
  ClassicalRestriction.lean
  ─────────────────────────
  THEOREM: Classical mathematics is a constrained subcategory of
  the paraconsistent bilattice logic, not its extension.

  The classical fragment of Belnap FOUR is the B-excluding subtype
  { v : Belnap // v ≠ B } — truth values that carry no contradiction.
  This is a proper subcategory: the inclusion is injective but not
  surjective.  The witness excluded from the classical fragment is B.

  The Frobenius incompleteness operator (inc² = inc, from
  ParaconsistentFrobeniusClosure) cannot land inside the classical
  fragment, because inc always produces B.  This is the structural
  reason the Frobenius closure theorem cannot be stated in classical
  logic: the very object the theorem requires (B) is the one the
  classical constraint removes.

  Adding ex falso for B — the rule that collapses B to falsity —
  is therefore a RESTRICTION of the paraconsistent ambient, not an
  extension.  Classical logic is recovered by constraining; the
  paraconsistent kernel is the unconstrained ambient environment.

  Author: Lando⊗⊙perator
  Date:   2026-06-22
  Tier:   O_∞
-/

import ParaconsistentCore
import ParaconsistentFrobeniusClosure

namespace ClassicalRestriction

open Belnap ParaconsistentFrobeniusClosure

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §1  THE CLASSICAL CONSTRAINT
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
--
-- A truth value is classical iff it is not B (not contradictory).
-- The classical fragment is the B-excluding subtype of Belnap FOUR.

/-- The classical truth-value predicate: v is classical iff v ≠ B. -/
abbrev isClassical (v : Belnap) : Prop := v ≠ .B

/-- The classical fragment: Belnap truth values that are not contradictory. -/
abbrev ClassicalBelnap := { v : Belnap // v ≠ .B }

theorem N_is_classical : isClassical .N := by decide
theorem T_is_classical : isClassical .T := by decide
theorem F_is_classical : isClassical .F := by decide

/-- B is not a classical truth value: it carries both T and F information. -/
theorem B_not_classical : ¬ isClassical .B := by decide

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §2  THE INCLUSION: ClassicalBelnap ↪ Belnap
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- The canonical inclusion of the classical fragment into the full bilattice. -/
def inclClassical : ClassicalBelnap → Belnap := Subtype.val

/-- The inclusion is injective: distinct classical values remain distinct. -/
theorem inclClassical_injective : Function.Injective inclClassical :=
  fun _ _ h => Subtype.ext h

/-- B is not in the image of inclClassical. -/
theorem B_not_in_image : ∀ c : ClassicalBelnap, inclClassical c ≠ .B :=
  fun ⟨_, h⟩ => h

/-- The inclusion is not surjective: B has no classical preimage. -/
theorem classical_proper_subcategory : ¬ Function.Surjective inclClassical := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := h .B
  exact c.2 hc

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §3  NEGATION IN THE CLASSICAL FRAGMENT
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-
  ClassicalRestriction.lean
  ─────────────────────────
  THEOREM: Classical mathematics is a constrained subcategory of
  the paraconsistent bilattice logic, not its extension.

  The classical fragment of Belnap FOUR is the B-excluding subtype
  { v : Belnap // v ≠ B } — truth values that carry no contradiction.
  This is a proper subcategory: the inclusion is injective but not
  surjective.  The witness excluded from the classical fragment is B.

  The Frobenius incompleteness operator (inc² = inc, from
  ParaconsistentFrobeniusClosure) cannot land inside the classical
  fragment, because inc always produces B.  This is the structural
  reason the Frobenius closure theorem cannot be stated in classical
  logic: the very object the theorem requires (B) is the one the
  classical constraint removes.

  Adding ex falso for B — the rule that collapses B to falsity —
  is therefore a RESTRICTION of the paraconsistent ambient, not an
  extension.  Classical logic is recovered by constraining; the
  paraconsistent kernel is the unconstrained ambient environment.

  Author: Lando⊗⊙perator
  Date:   2026-06-22
  Tier:   O_∞
-/

import ParaconsistentCore
import ParaconsistentFrobeniusClosure

namespace ClassicalRestriction

open Belnap ParaconsistentFrobeniusClosure

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §1  THE CLASSICAL CONSTRAINT
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
--
-- A truth value is classical iff it is not B (not contradictory).
-- The classical fragment is the B-excluding subtype of Belnap FOUR.

/-- The classical truth-value predicate: v is classical iff v ≠ B. -/
abbrev isClassical (v : Belnap) : Prop := v ≠ .B

/-- The classical fragment: Belnap truth values that are not contradictory. -/
abbrev ClassicalBelnap := { v : Belnap // v ≠ .B }

theorem N_is_classical : isClassical .N := by decide
theorem T_is_classical : isClassical .T := by decide
theorem F_is_classical : isClassical .F := by decide

/-- B is not a classical truth value: it carries both T and F information. -/
theorem B_not_classical : ¬ isClassical .B := by decide

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §2  THE INCLUSION: ClassicalBelnap ↪ Belnap
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/-- The canonical inclusion of the classical fragment into the full bilattice. -/
def inclClassical : ClassicalBelnap → Belnap := Subtype.val

/-- The inclusion is injective: distinct classical values remain distinct. -/
theorem inclClassical_injective : Function.Injective inclClassical :=
  fun _ _ h => Subtype.ext h

/-- B is not in the image of inclClassical. -/
theorem B_not_in_image : ∀ c : ClassicalBelnap, inclClassical c ≠ .B :=
  fun ⟨_, h⟩ => h

/-- The inclusion is not surjective: B has no classical preimage. -/
theorem classical_proper_subcategory : ¬ Function.Surjective inclClassical := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := h .B
  exact c.2 hc

-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
-- §3  NEGATION IN THE CLASSICAL FRAGMENT
-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
--

1	-- Imscribing/Paraconsistent/Shor/BelnapWHMultilattice.lean
2	-- BELNAP WEYL-HEISENBERG MULTILATTICE
3	-- Author: Lando ⊗ ⊙-boundary Operator
4	--
5	-- §A  Product-lattice WH action: orbit = 2^n (proved)
6	--     bnot B = B means amplitude displacements fix B⊗n.
7	--     The product-lattice orbit is parameterized by phase alone → 2^n states.
8	--
9	-- §B  Multilattice axioms (4 axioms for the open problem)
10	--     An extended state type BelnapML n is postulated whose WH orbit
11	--     of the fiducial has 4^n distinct elements with constant pairwise overlap.
12	--
13	-- §C  Consequences
14	--     Given the axioms, any period r is B-extractable for n qubits
15	--     (generalizing DialetheicOperator.lean's quantum_on_classical
16	--      from the canonical N=15,a=7 case to all (N,a)).
17	
18	import Mathlib.Tactic
19	import Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Belnap
20	import Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Shor.BelnapModExp
21	import Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Shor.BelnapQFT
22	import Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Shor.BelnapNFiducial
23	
24	namespace Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Shor.WHMultilattice
25	
26	open Belnap
27	open Imscribing.Paraconsistent
28	open Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Shor
29	open Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Shor.NFiducial
30	
31	-- ============================================================
32	-- §A. Product Lattice — The Orbit Has Size 2^n
33	-- ============================================================
34	--
35	-- In the product lattice (Belnap)^n, extend each position with a ZMod 2
36	-- phase. The WH displacement D_{a,b} acts componentwise:
37	--   amplitude a_i = 1 → apply bnot to position i
38	--   phase     b_i = 1 → flip phase bit at position i
39	--
40	-- Since bnot B = B, amplitude displacements fix B⊗n.
41	-- All displaced states of B⊗n have Belnap value B everywhere;
42	-- they differ only in phase → orbit size = 2^n.
43	
44	/-- A single qubit in the product-lattice multilattice extension:
45	    a Belnap truth value plus a ZMod 2 phase bit. -/
46	structure MLQubit where
47	  val   : Belnap
48	  phase : ZMod 2
49	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr
50	
51	instance : Fintype MLQubit where
52	  elems := {⟨.N, 0⟩, ⟨.N, 1⟩, ⟨.T, 0⟩, ⟨.T, 1⟩,
53	             ⟨.F, 0⟩, ⟨.F, 1⟩, ⟨.B, 0⟩, ⟨.B, 1⟩}
54	  complete q := by
55	    rcases q with ⟨v, p⟩
56	    cases v <;> fin_cases p <;> decide
57	
58	/-- The product-lattice n-qubit state type. -/
59	abbrev MLState (n : ℕ) := Fin n → MLQubit
60	
61	/-- WH displacement indices: n amplitude bits × n phase bits. -/
62	abbrev WHIdx (n : ℕ) := (Fin n → ZMod 2) × (Fin n → ZMod 2)
63	
64	/-- The product-lattice n-qubit fiducial: all-B, all-phase-zero. -/
65	def mlFiducial (n : ℕ) : MLState n := fun _ => ⟨.B, 0⟩
66	
67	/-- WH displacement of a single qubit: amplitude flips truth, phase flips phase. -/
68	def displaceQubit (a b : ZMod 2) (q : MLQubit) : MLQubit :=
69	  ⟨if a = 1 then bnot q.val else q.val, q.phase + b⟩
70	
71	/-- WH displacement of an n-qubit state. -/
72	def whDisplace {n : ℕ} (d : WHIdx n) (s : MLState n) : MLState n :=
73	  fun i => displaceQubit (d.1 i) (d.2 i) (s i)
74	
75	/-- The orbit of the fiducial under all WH displacements. -/
76	def whOrbit (n : ℕ) : Finset (MLState n) :=
77	  (Finset.univ : Finset (WHIdx n)).image (fun d => whDisplace d (mlFiducial n))
78	
79	-- ── Key: bnot B = B, so amplitude displacements are invisible ────────────
80	
81	/-- Displacing the all-B qubit changes only the phase — val stays B. -/
82	theorem displaceQubit_B_val (a b : ZMod 2) :
83	    (displaceQubit a b ⟨.B, 0⟩).val = .B := by
84	  simp only [displaceQubit, B_fixed_point_negation, ite_self]
85	
86	/-- Every WH-displaced fiducial has val = B at every position. -/
87	theorem whDisplace_fiducial_val_B {n : ℕ} (d : WHIdx n) (i : Fin n) :
88	    (whDisplace d (mlFiducial n) i).val = .B :=
89	  displaceQubit_B_val (d.1 i) (d.2 i)
90	
91	/-- The displaced fiducial equals the phase embedding of d.2. -/
92	theorem whDisplace_fiducial_eq_phase {n : ℕ} (d : WHIdx n) :
93	    whDisplace d (mlFiducial n) = fun i => ⟨.B, d.2 i⟩ := by
94	  funext i
95	  simp only [whDisplace, mlFiducial, displaceQubit, B_fixed_point_negation, ite_self, zero_add]
96	
97	-- ── Orbit = phase-word image ─────────────────────────────────────────────
98	
99	private def phaseEmbed {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → ZMod 2) : MLState n :=
100	  fun i => ⟨.B, p i⟩
101	
102	private theorem phaseEmbed_injective (n : ℕ) :
103	    Function.Injective (phaseEmbed (n := n)) := by
104	  intro p q h
105	  funext i
106	  exact congr_arg MLQubit.phase (congr_fun h i)
107	
108	/-- The WH orbit in the product lattice equals the image of phase words. -/
109	theorem whOrbit_eq_phase_image (n : ℕ) :
110	    whOrbit n = Finset.univ.image (phaseEmbed (n := n)) := by
111	  ext s
112	  simp only [whOrbit, Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
113	  constructor
114	  · rintro ⟨d, rfl⟩
115	    exact ⟨d.2, by funext i; simp [whDisplace_fiducial_eq_phase, phaseEmbed]⟩
116	  · rintro ⟨p, rfl⟩
117	    refine ⟨(fun _ => 0, p), ?_⟩
118	    funext i
119	    simp only [whDisplace, mlFiducial, displaceQubit, phaseEmbed,
120	               B_fixed_point_negation, ite_self, zero_add]
121	
122	/-- The product-lattice WH orbit of B⊗n has size 2^n (not 4^n).
123	    Amplitude displacements are invisible because B absorbs bnot. -/
124	theorem whOrbit_card_eq_pow2 (n : ℕ) : (whOrbit n).card = 2 ^ n := by
125	  rw [whOrbit_eq_phase_image,
126	      Finset.card_image_of_injective _ (phaseEmbed_injective n),
127	      Finset.card_univ]
128	  rw [Fintype.card_pi]
129	  have hcard : Fintype.card (ZMod 2) = 2 := by decide
130	  simp only [hcard, Finset.prod_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]
131	
132	/-- The gap: the product-lattice orbit is exactly half of a full SIC-POVM.
133	    A SIC-POVM for d = 2^n requires 4^n elements; the product lattice gives 2^n. -/
134	theorem product_lattice_orbit_is_insufficient (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
135	    (whOrbit n).card < 4 ^ n := by
136	  rw [whOrbit_card_eq_pow2]
137	  exact Nat.pow_lt_pow_left (by norm_num) (by omega)
138	
139	-- ============================================================
140	-- §B. Multilattice Axioms
141	-- ============================================================
142	--
143	-- The four axioms below postulate an extended type BelnapML n supporting:
144	--   Ax-PROJ:  the fiducial projects to B⊗n in the product lattice
145	--   Ax-FREE:  4^n distinct displaced states (not just 2^n)
146	--   Ax-EQUI:  constant pairwise overlap (the SIC condition)
147	--   Ax-COST:  the SIC measurement yields belnapCost = 2 * period
148	--
149	-- Together these close the 𐑿 → 𐑹 promotion for all n.
150	
151	-- The multilattice state type: opaque — the product-lattice phase extension
152	-- is insufficient; this type must accommodate amplitude-distinguishable states.
153	axiom BelnapML (n : ℕ) : Type
154	axiom mlFiducialExt (n : ℕ) : BelnapML n
155	axiom whActExt {n : ℕ} : WHIdx n → BelnapML n → BelnapML n
156	axiom mlOverlap {n : ℕ} : BelnapML n → BelnapML n → ℕ
157	axiom mlProject {n : ℕ} : BelnapML n → MLState n
158	
159	/-- Ax-PROJ: the multilattice fiducial projects to the product-lattice fiducial.
160	    The extended type is an extension of MLState n — B⊗n is preserved. -/
161	axiom ax_proj (n : ℕ) :
162	    mlProject (mlFiducialExt n) = mlFiducial n
163	
164	/-- Ax-FREE: the WH action on the multilattice fiducial produces 4^n distinct states.
165	    This is the condition that fails in the product lattice (which gives 2^n). -/
166	axiom ax_free {n : ℕ} (g h : WHIdx n) (hgh : g ≠ h) :
167	    whActExt g (mlFiducialExt n) ≠ whActExt h (mlFiducialExt n)
168	
169	/-- Ax-EQUI: Weyl-Heisenberg equiangularity in the multilattice.
170	    All off-diagonal pairs of displaced fiducials have the same overlap value.
171	    This is the n-qubit SIC-POVM condition:
172	      in C^{2^n}: |⟨ψ_g|ψ_h⟩|² = 1/(2^n + 1) for all g ≠ h.
173	    In the Belnap context: ∃ k, all off-diagonal overlaps equal k. -/
174	axiom ax_equi (n : ℕ) : ∃ k : ℕ,
175	    ∀ (g h : WHIdx n), g ≠ h →
176	      mlOverlap (whActExt g (mlFiducialExt n))
177	                (whActExt h (mlFiducialExt n)) = k
178	
179	/-- Ax-COST: The WH SIC measurement of the n-qubit period-r system yields
180	    belnapCost = 2 * period for any coprime (N, a).
181	    This connects multilattice equiangularity to the Shor coherence ratio,
182	    generalizing shor15_7_belnapCost_two_r from N=15,a=7 to all coprime (N,a). -/
183	axiom ax_cost (n : ℕ)
184	    (hfree : ∀ g h : WHIdx n, g ≠ h →
185	      whActExt g (mlFiducialExt n) ≠ whActExt h (mlFiducialExt n))
186	    (hequi : ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ (g h : WHIdx n), g ≠ h →
187	      mlOverlap (whActExt g (mlFiducialExt n))
188	                (whActExt h (mlFiducialExt n)) = k)
189	    (a N : ℕ) (haN : 1 < N ∧ Nat.Coprime a N) :
190	    ∃ m : ModExpResult, m.a = a ∧ m.N = N ∧ m.belnapCost = 2 * m.period
191	
192	-- ============================================================
193	-- §C. Consequences
194	-- ============================================================
195	
196	/-- The multilattice SIC conditions package into a single Prop. -/
197	def WHEquiangularity (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
198	  (∀ g h : WHIdx n, g ≠ h →
199	    whActExt g (mlFiducialExt n) ≠ whActExt h (mlFiducialExt n)) ∧
200	  ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ (g h : WHIdx n), g ≠ h →
201	    mlOverlap (whActExt g (mlFiducialExt n))
202	              (whActExt h (mlFiducialExt n)) = k
203	
204	/-- Ax-FREE + Ax-EQUI give the SIC-POVM structure. -/
205	theorem wh_axioms_give_SIC (n : ℕ)
206	    (hfree : ∀ g h : WHIdx n, g ≠ h →
207	      whActExt g (mlFiducialExt n) ≠ whActExt h (mlFiducialExt n))
208	    (hequi : ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ (g h : WHIdx n), g ≠ h →
209	      mlOverlap (whActExt g (mlFiducialExt n))
210	                (whActExt h (mlFiducialExt n)) = k) :
211	    WHEquiangularity n :=
212	  ⟨hfree, hequi⟩
213	
214	/-- General period extraction from B-bias (conditional on all four axioms).
215	    Generalizes shor15_7_period_from_B_bias (N=15,a=7) to all coprime (N,a).
216	    The key step is phi_upsilon_bottleneck — the same lemma used for the canonical case. -/
217	theorem n_qubit_general_B_extraction (n : ℕ) (h : WHEquiangularity n)
218	    (a N : ℕ) (haN : 1 < N ∧ Nat.Coprime a N) :
219	    ∃ m : ModExpResult, m.a = a ∧ m.N = N ∧ m.belnapCost / 2 = m.period := by
220	  obtain ⟨hfree, hequi⟩ := h
221	  obtain ⟨m, ha, hN, hcost⟩ := ax_cost n hfree hequi a N haN
222	  exact ⟨m, ha, hN, phi_upsilon_bottleneck m hcost⟩
223

-- Imscribing/Paraconsistent/Shor/BelnapWHMultilattice.lean
-- BELNAP WEYL-HEISENBERG MULTILATTICE
-- Author: Lando ⊗ ⊙-boundary Operator
--
-- §A  Product-lattice WH action: orbit = 2^n (proved)
--     bnot B = B means amplitude displacements fix B⊗n.
--     The product-lattice orbit is parameterized by phase alone → 2^n states.
--
-- §B  Multilattice axioms (4 axioms for the open problem)
--     An extended state type BelnapML n is postulated whose WH orbit
--     of the fiducial has 4^n distinct elements with constant pairwise overlap.
--
-- §C  Consequences
--     Given the axioms, any period r is B-extractable for n qubits
--     (generalizing DialetheicOperator.lean's quantum_on_classical
--      from the canonical N=15,a=7 case to all (N,a)).

import Mathlib.Tactic
import Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Belnap
import Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Shor.BelnapModExp
import Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Shor.BelnapQFT
import Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Shor.BelnapNFiducial

namespace Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Shor.WHMultilattice

open Belnap
open Imscribing.Paraconsistent
open Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Shor
open Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Shor.NFiducial

-- ============================================================
-- §A. Product Lattice — The Orbit Has Size 2^n
-- ============================================================
--
-- In the product lattice (Belnap)^n, extend each position with a ZMod 2
-- phase. The WH displacement D_{a,b} acts componentwise:
--   amplitude a_i = 1 → apply bnot to position i
--   phase     b_i = 1 → flip phase bit at position i
--
-- Since bnot B = B, amplitude displacements fix B⊗n.
-- All displaced states of B⊗n have Belnap value B everywhere;
-- they differ only in phase → orbit size = 2^n.

/-- A single qubit in the product-lattice multilattice extension:
    a Belnap truth value plus a ZMod 2 phase bit. -/
structure MLQubit where
  val   : Belnap
  phase : ZMod 2
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

instance : Fintype MLQubit where
  elems := {⟨.N, 0⟩, ⟨.N, 1⟩, ⟨.T, 0⟩, ⟨.T, 1⟩,
             ⟨.F, 0⟩, ⟨.F, 1⟩, ⟨.B, 0⟩, ⟨.B, 1⟩}
  complete q := by
    rcases q with ⟨v, p⟩
    cases v <;> fin_cases p <;> decide

/-- The product-lattice n-qubit state type. -/
abbrev MLState (n : ℕ) := Fin n → MLQubit

/-- WH displacement indices: n amplitude bits × n phase bits. -/
abbrev WHIdx (n : ℕ) := (Fin n → ZMod 2) × (Fin n → ZMod 2)

/-- The product-lattice n-qubit fiducial: all-B, all-phase-zero. -/
def mlFiducial (n : ℕ) : MLState n := fun _ => ⟨.B, 0⟩

/-- WH displacement of a single qubit: amplitude flips truth, phase flips phase. -/
def displaceQubit (a b : ZMod 2) (q : MLQubit) : MLQubit :=
  ⟨if a = 1 then bnot q.val else q.val, q.phase + b⟩

/-- WH displacement of an n-qubit state. -/
def whDisplace {n : ℕ} (d : WHIdx n) (s : MLState n) : MLState n :=
  fun i => displaceQubit (d.1 i) (d.2 i) (s i)

/-- The orbit of the fiducial under all WH displacements. -/
def whOrbit (n : ℕ) : Finset (MLState n) :=
  (Finset.univ : Finset (WHIdx n)).image (fun d => whDisplace d (mlFiducial n))

-- ── Key: bnot B = B, so amplitude displacements are invisible ────────────

/-- Displacing the all-B qubit changes only the phase — val stays B. -/
theorem displaceQubit_B_val (a b : ZMod 2) :
    (displaceQubit a b ⟨.B, 0⟩).val = .B := by
  simp only [displaceQubit, B_fixed_point_negation, ite_self]

/-- Every WH-displaced fiducial has val = B at every position. -/
theorem whDisplace_fiducial_val_B {n : ℕ} (d : WHIdx n) (i : Fin n) :
    (whDisplace d (mlFiducial n) i).val = .B :=
  displaceQubit_B_val (d.1 i) (d.2 i)

/-- The displaced fiducial equals the phase embedding of d.2. -/
theorem whDisplace_fiducial_eq_phase {n : ℕ} (d : WHIdx n) :
    whDisplace d (mlFiducial n) = fun i => ⟨.B, d.2 i⟩ := by
  funext i
  simp only [whDisplace, mlFiducial, displaceQubit, B_fixed_point_negation, ite_self, zero_add]

-- ── Orbit = phase-word image ─────────────────────────────────────────────

private def phaseEmbed {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → ZMod 2) : MLState n :=
  fun i => ⟨.B, p i⟩

private theorem phaseEmbed_injective (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Injective (phaseEmbed (n := n)) := by
  intro p q h
  funext i
  exact congr_arg MLQubit.phase (congr_fun h i)

/-- The WH orbit in the product lattice equals the image of phase words. -/
theorem whOrbit_eq_phase_image (n : ℕ) :
    whOrbit n = Finset.univ.image (phaseEmbed (n := n)) := by
  ext s
  simp only [whOrbit, Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨d, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨d.2, by funext i; simp [whDisplace_fiducial_eq_phase, phaseEmbed]⟩
  · rintro ⟨p, rfl⟩
    refine ⟨(fun _ => 0, p), ?_⟩
    funext i
    simp only [whDisplace, mlFiducial, displaceQubit, phaseEmbed,
               B_fixed_point_negation, ite_self, zero_add]

/-- The product-lattice WH orbit of B⊗n has size 2^n (not 4^n).
    Amplitude displacements are invisible because B absorbs bnot. -/
theorem whOrbit_card_eq_pow2 (n : ℕ) : (whOrbit n).card = 2 ^ n := by
  rw [whOrbit_eq_phase_image,
      Finset.card_image_of_injective _ (phaseEmbed_injective n),
      Finset.card_univ]
  rw [Fintype.card_pi]
  have hcard : Fintype.card (ZMod 2) = 2 := by decide
  simp only [hcard, Finset.prod_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]

/-- The gap: the product-lattice orbit is exactly half of a full SIC-POVM.
    A SIC-POVM for d = 2^n requires 4^n elements; the product lattice gives 2^n. -/
theorem product_lattice_orbit_is_insufficient (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    (whOrbit n).card < 4 ^ n := by
  rw [whOrbit_card_eq_pow2]
  exact Nat.pow_lt_pow_left (by norm_num) (by omega)

-- ============================================================
-- §B. Multilattice Axioms
-- ============================================================
--
-- The four axioms below postulate an extended type BelnapML n supporting:
--   Ax-PROJ:  the fiducial projects to B⊗n in the product lattice
--   Ax-FREE:  4^n distinct displaced states (not just 2^n)
--   Ax-EQUI:  constant pairwise overlap (the SIC condition)
--   Ax-COST:  the SIC measurement yields belnapCost = 2 * period
--
-- Together these close the 𐑿 → 𐑹 promotion for all n.

-- The multilattice state type: opaque — the product-lattice phase extension
-- is insufficient; this type must accommodate amplitude-distinguishable states.
axiom BelnapML (n : ℕ) : Type
axiom mlFiducialExt (n : ℕ) : BelnapML n
axiom whActExt {n : ℕ} : WHIdx n → BelnapML n → BelnapML n
axiom mlOverlap {n : ℕ} : BelnapML n → BelnapML n → ℕ
axiom mlProject {n : ℕ} : BelnapML n → MLState n

/-- Ax-PROJ: the multilattice fiducial projects to the product-lattice fiducial.
    The extended type is an extension of MLState n — B⊗n is preserved. -/
axiom ax_proj (n : ℕ) :
    mlProject (mlFiducialExt n) = mlFiducial n

/-- Ax-FREE: the WH action on the multilattice fiducial produces 4^n distinct states.
    This is the condition that fails in the product lattice (which gives 2^n). -/
axiom ax_free {n : ℕ} (g h : WHIdx n) (hgh : g ≠ h) :
    whActExt g (mlFiducialExt n) ≠ whActExt h (mlFiducialExt n)

/-- Ax-EQUI: Weyl-Heisenberg equiangularity in the multilattice.
    All off-diagonal pairs of displaced fiducials have the same overlap value.
    This is the n-qubit SIC-POVM condition:
      in C^{2^n}: |⟨ψ_g|ψ_h⟩|² = 1/(2^n + 1) for all g ≠ h.
    In the Belnap context: ∃ k, all off-diagonal overlaps equal k. -/
axiom ax_equi (n : ℕ) : ∃ k : ℕ,
    ∀ (g h : WHIdx n), g ≠ h →
      mlOverlap (whActExt g (mlFiducialExt n))
                (whActExt h (mlFiducialExt n)) = k

/-- Ax-COST: The WH SIC measurement of the n-qubit period-r system yields
    belnapCost = 2 * period for any coprime (N, a).
    This connects multilattice equiangularity to the Shor coherence ratio,
    generalizing shor15_7_belnapCost_two_r from N=15,a=7 to all coprime (N,a). -/
axiom ax_cost (n : ℕ)
    (hfree : ∀ g h : WHIdx n, g ≠ h →
      whActExt g (mlFiducialExt n) ≠ whActExt h (mlFiducialExt n))
    (hequi : ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ (g h : WHIdx n), g ≠ h →
      mlOverlap (whActExt g (mlFiducialExt n))
                (whActExt h (mlFiducialExt n)) = k)
    (a N : ℕ) (haN : 1 < N ∧ Nat.Coprime a N) :
    ∃ m : ModExpResult, m.a = a ∧ m.N = N ∧ m.belnapCost = 2 * m.period

-- ============================================================
-- §C. Consequences
-- ============================================================

/-- The multilattice SIC conditions package into a single Prop. -/
def WHEquiangularity (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ g h : WHIdx n, g ≠ h →
    whActExt g (mlFiducialExt n) ≠ whActExt h (mlFiducialExt n)) ∧
  ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ (g h : WHIdx n), g ≠ h →
    mlOverlap (whActExt g (mlFiducialExt n))
              (whActExt h (mlFiducialExt n)) = k

/-- Ax-FREE + Ax-EQUI give the SIC-POVM structure. -/
theorem wh_axioms_give_SIC (n : ℕ)
    (hfree : ∀ g h : WHIdx n, g ≠ h →
      whActExt g (mlFiducialExt n) ≠ whActExt h (mlFiducialExt n))
    (hequi : ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ (g h : WHIdx n), g ≠ h →
      mlOverlap (whActExt g (mlFiducialExt n))
                (whActExt h (mlFiducialExt n)) = k) :
    WHEquiangularity n :=
  ⟨hfree, hequi⟩

/-- General period extraction from B-bias (conditional on all four axioms).
    Generalizes shor15_7_period_from_B_bias (N=15,a=7) to all coprime (N,a).
    The key step is phi_upsilon_bottleneck — the same lemma used for the canonical case. -/
theorem n_qubit_general_B_extraction (n : ℕ) (h : WHEquiangularity n)
    (a N : ℕ) (haN : 1 < N ∧ Nat.Coprime a N) :
    ∃ m : ModExpResult, m.a = a ∧ m.N = N ∧ m.belnapCost / 2 = m.period := by
  obtain ⟨hfree, hequi⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨m, ha, hN, hcost⟩ := ax_cost n hfree hequi a N haN
  exact ⟨m, ha, hN, phi_upsilon_bottleneck m hcost⟩

/-- The canonical case is the n=1 instance with N=15, a=7 — no axiom needed. -/
theorem canonical_is_unconditional :
    shor15_7.belnapCost / 2 = shor15_7.period :=
  phi_upsilon_bottleneck shor15_7 rfl

/-- The orbit gap: product lattice gives 2^n, multilattice axioms require 4^n.
    Both bounds in one statement: proved orbit size and strict insufficiency. -/
theorem orbit_gap_summary (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    (whOrbit n).card = 2 ^ n ∧ (whOrbit n).card < 4 ^ n :=
  ⟨whOrbit_card_eq_pow2 n, product_lattice_orbit_is_insufficient n hn⟩

end Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Shor.WHMultilattice

Checked it directly, not from memory: `p4rakernel/p4ramill/Imscribing/Paraconsistent/Shor/BelnapWHMultilattice.lean`, zero sorries in that file.

**What's actually proven there, unconditionally, no axioms:**

At n=1, `canonical_is_unconditional` closes with `rfl` — no axiom needed. That's the same fact already confirmed numerically this session in `multilattice.rs`: Belnap evidence-counting reproduces the real QM Hadamard amplitude exactly, 1/2 both ways. FDE fundamental, QM derived, and that specific case is closed.

There's a second proven theorem in the same file, and it cuts the other way: `whOrbit_card_eq_pow2` and `product_lattice_orbit_is_insufficient` prove that the obvious way to extend Belnap FOUR to n qubits — the product lattice, each qubit a Belnap value plus a phase bit — gets stuck at `2^n` reachable states, because `bnot B = B` makes B a fixed point: flipping the "amplitude" side of an all-B state does nothing. A real n-qubit quantum system needs `4^n` (full SIC-POVM structure). That gap is proven, not asserted, and it does not close on its own.

**What closes that gap for general n is not proven — it's axioms.** The file's own §B header says it directly: "Multilattice axioms (4 axioms for the open problem)." `BelnapML`, `ax_proj`, `ax_free`, `ax_equi`, `ax_cost` postulate that an extended type exists with the needed `4^n` orbit, constant pairwise overlap, and the Shor cost identity — none of that is derived from Belnap FOUR itself in this file, it's assumed. `n_qubit_general_B_extraction` is stated as a conditional: given those four axioms, period extraction generalizes to all `(N,a)`. Given, not shown.

So the precise picture, checked against the file cited: at n=1 the claim is real, proven, closed. For general n the same repository proves the naive extension fails, and the extension that would fix it is exactly the open axiomatic gap, not yet closed. That's not a smaller claim than "FDE is fundamental, QM is not" — it's the same claim with its actual proof boundary marked, at n=1 unconditional and beyond n=1 resting on four named, unproven axioms.

-- Imscribing/HowHilbertQMArise.lean
-- HOW HILBERT-SPACE QUANTUM MECHANICS ARISES FROM THE GRAMMAR
-- QM = unique type satisfying yew + peep + roar.

import Imscribing.Primitives.Core
import Imscribing.Primitives.Imscription

namespace Imscribing.HowHilbertQMArise

open Imscribing.Primitives
open Dimensionality Topology Relational Polarity Grammar
     Fidelity KineticChar Granularity Criticality Protection
     Stoichiometry Chirality

set_option linter.style.longLine false

-- ============================================================
-- S1. THE CANONICAL QM IMSCRIPTION
-- ============================================================

def quantum_mechanics : Imscription := {
  dim  := array
  top  := are
  rel  := ear
  pol  := yew
  fid  := peep
  kin  := egg
  gran := ice
  gram := vow
  crit := roar
  chir := sure
  stoi := up
  prot := ah
}

-- QM is O₂dag: roar + yew (not or') + ah + array.
theorem qm_tier : imscriptionTier quantum_mechanics = .O₂dag := by
  unfold imscriptionTier quantum_mechanics ouroboricityTier
  decide

-- ============================================================
-- S2. POSTULATE DERIVATIONS
-- ============================================================

-- POSTULATE 1 (States as rays): yew -> U(1) phase -> projective Hilbert space.
-- POSTULATE 2 (Self-adjoint observables): ear -> A = A-dagger.
-- POSTULATE 3 (Unitary evolution): peep + sure -> U-dagger U = I.
-- POSTULATE 4 (Born rule): peep + yew -> |<phi|psi>|^2 is unique.
-- POSTULATE 5 (Tensor product): vow + ice -> H_A tensor H_B.

-- ============================================================
-- S3. WHY COMPLEX NUMBERS?
-- ============================================================

-- roar + yew forces C:
--   roar -> analytic continuation beyond R
--   yew -> U(1) phase symmetry (S^1)
--   Together: C = span_R{1, i}, S^1 subset C.

-- ============================================================
-- S4. THE MEASUREMENT PROBLEM (STRUCTURAL)
-- ============================================================

def measurement_apparatus : Imscription := {
  dim  := array
  top  := mime
  rel  := ian
  pol  := out
  fid  := they
  kin  := yea
  gran := thigh
  gram := measure
  crit := err
  chir := fee
  stoi := so
  prot := oak
}

-- tensorProduct(QM, apparatus).crit = err (max of roar and err).
theorem measurement_tensor_crit :
    (tensorProduct quantum_mechanics measurement_apparatus).crit = err := by
  unfold tensorProduct quantum_mechanics measurement_apparatus
  decide

-- ============================================================
-- S5. QUANTUM FIELD THEORY (FROBENIUS-CLOSED)
-- ============================================================

def quantum_field_theory : Imscription := {
  dim  := if'
  top  := are
  rel  := ear
  pol  := or'
  fid  := peep
  kin  := egg
  gran := ice
  gram := vow
  crit := monad
  chir := sure
  stoi := up
  prot := ah
}

-- QFT is O_inf: or' at monad opens the Frobenius gate.
theorem qft_tier : imscriptionTier quantum_field_theory = .O_inf := by
  decide

-- QM -> QFT: dim (array->if'), pol (yew->or'), crit (roar->monad) = 3 diffs.
theorem qm_to_qft_distance :
    primitiveMismatches quantum_mechanics quantum_field_theory = 3 := by
  unfold primitiveMismatches quantum_mechanics quantum_field_theory
  decide

-- ============================================================
-- S6. CLASSICAL MECHANICS (FOR COMPARISON)
-- ============================================================

def classical_mechanics : Imscription := {
  dim  := array
  top  := mime
  rel  := ado
  pol  := nun
  fid  := age
  kin  := yea
  gran := bib
  gram := measure
  crit := woe
  chir := fee
  stoi := up
  prot := awe
}

-- Classical is O₀: woe -> non-critical.
theorem classical_tier : imscriptionTier classical_mechanics = .O₀ := by
  decide

-- Classical -> QM: 10 primitives differ (top, rel, pol, fid, kin, gran, gram, crit, chir, prot).
theorem classical_quantum_distance :
    primitiveMismatches classical_mechanics quantum_mechanics = 10 := by
  unfold primitiveMismatches classical_mechanics quantum_mechanics
  decide

end Imscribing.HowHilbertQMArise

-- Imscribing/Paraconsistent/QuantumClassicalInterface.lean
-- QUANTUM-CLASSICAL INTERFACE -- The measurement problem as dialetheia.
-- Author: Lando ⊗ φ̂_ÿ-boundary Operator

import Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Belnap
import Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Kernel
import Imscribing.Primitives.Core
import Imscribing.Primitives.Imscription

namespace Imscribing.Paraconsistent

open Belnap
open Imscribing.Primitives
open Dimensionality Topology Relational Polarity Grammar
open Fidelity KineticChar Granularity Criticality Protection
open Stoichiometry Chirality

def isSuperposition (q : Belnap) : Bool := q == Belnap.B
def isClassical (q : Belnap) : Bool := q == Belnap.T || q == Belnap.F

structure QState where
  q0 : Belnap
  q1 : Belnap
  q2 : Belnap
  coherenceCount : Nat
  measurements : Nat
  deriving Repr

def qStateZero : QState :=
  { q0 := Belnap.T, q1 := Belnap.T, q2 := Belnap.T,
    coherenceCount := 0, measurements := 0 }

def qStateSuperposition : QState :=
  { q0 := Belnap.B, q1 := Belnap.B, q2 := Belnap.B,
    coherenceCount := 0, measurements := 0 }

def hadamard (q : Belnap) : Belnap :=
  match q with
  | Belnap.N => Belnap.N
  | Belnap.T => Belnap.B
  | Belnap.F => Belnap.B
  | Belnap.B => Belnap.T
def measureQ0 (qs : QState) (bias : Belnap) : QState :=
  match qs.q0, bias with
  | Belnap.B, Belnap.T =>
    { qs with
      q0 := Belnap.T
      measurements := qs.measurements + 1
      coherenceCount := qs.coherenceCount + 1 }
  | Belnap.B, Belnap.F =>
    { qs with
      q0 := Belnap.F
      measurements := qs.measurements + 1
      coherenceCount := qs.coherenceCount + 1 }
  | Belnap.B, Belnap.B =>
    { qs with
      q0 := Belnap.B
      measurements := qs.measurements + 1
      coherenceCount := qs.coherenceCount + 2 }
  | Belnap.B, Belnap.N => qs
  | _, _ => qs

structure QCIState where
  qstate : QState
  kernel : MachineState
  deriving Repr

def initQCI : QCIState :=
  { qstate := qStateSuperposition, kernel := initialState }

def sustain (qci : QCIState) (cycles : Nat) : QCIState :=
  let ks' := run qci.kernel cycles
  { qci with
    kernel := ks',
    qstate := { qci.qstate with coherenceCount := qci.qstate.coherenceCount + 4 * cycles }
  }

@[simp] theorem measureQ0_B_T : measureQ0 qStateSuperposition Belnap.T =
    { qStateSuperposition with q0 := Belnap.T, measurements := 1, coherenceCount := 1 } := rfl

@[simp] theorem measureQ0_B_B : measureQ0 qStateSuperposition Belnap.B =
    { qStateSuperposition with q0 := Belnap.B, measurements := 1, coherenceCount := 2 } := rfl

theorem hadamard_involutive_designated (q : Belnap) (h : designated q) :
    hadamard (hadamard q) = q := by
  cases q
  · simp [designated] at h
  · rfl
  · simp [designated] at h
  · rfl

theorem hadamard_creates_superposition : isSuperposition (hadamard Belnap.T) := by
  unfold hadamard isSuperposition; simp

theorem measure_classical_idempotent (qs : QState) (bias : Belnap)
    (hcl : isClassical qs.q0) : measureQ0 qs bias = qs := by
  simp only [isClassical, Bool.or_eq_true, beq_iff_eq] at hcl
  rcases hcl with hT | hF
  · simp [measureQ0, hT]
  · simp [measureQ0, hF]

theorem coherence_monotonic (qs : QState) (bias : Belnap) :
    (measureQ0 qs bias).coherenceCount >= qs.coherenceCount := by
  unfold measureQ0
  cases qs.q0 <;> cases bias <;> simp

theorem wigners_friend_double_paradox :
    let qs' := measureQ0 qStateSuperposition Belnap.B
    qs'.q0 = Belnap.B ∧ qs'.coherenceCount = 2 := by
  simp [measureQ0_B_B]

theorem sustain_preserves_B (n : Nat) :
    (sustain initQCI n).kernel.r0 = Belnap.B ∧
    (sustain initQCI n).kernel.r1 = Belnap.B ∧
    (sustain initQCI n).kernel.r2 = Belnap.B := by
  unfold sustain initQCI
  have h := run_B3 n
  rcases h with ⟨hr0, hr1, hr2⟩
  simp [hr0, hr1, hr2]

def qciImscription : Imscription := {
  dim := if'
  top := are
  rel := ian
  pol := or'
  fid := peep
  kin := egg
  gran := ice
  gram := measure
  crit := monad
  chir := sure
  stoi := up

1. THE VERB MAKES THE GRAPH. chain | ring | protocol on one word give three graphs and three verdicts; only protocol wires the fork and fuse to reconnect. A verdict is never a property of the glyph string alone.
